personalInfo.name: Edmund
personalInfo.title: Mechanical Engineering Student
personalInfo.longDescription: I grew up in Kuching, a small city on the island of Borneo. As a kid I always dreamt of leaving home to explore beyond my horizons, and I've been fortunate enough to study mechanical engineering at two of the world's best universities. At UCL I'm on track for First Class Honours, and in 2025 I won the Frederic Barnes Waldron Best Student Award, given to the student with the highest year average across the whole university. I spent my third year on exchange at UC Berkeley and finished with a 4.00 GPA. Outside of the classroom, I spent a year researching photon detector cooling at Berkeley's FLOW Lab, and wrote a paper under Prof. Liwei Lin studying the use of nanowires in solid-state thermoelectric cooling. On the competitive side, I was the recovery systems lead for UCL Rocketry's entries at the Spaceport America Cup (SAC) 2025 and the National Rocketry Championship (NRC) 2024. Closest to my heart is the Sarawak Student Initiative, which I started in 2021. Education opportunities in my home state are nowhere near equal, and I know how much difference one person's guidance can make. SSI exists so that every student in Sarawak, wherever they start from, gets a real chance to go out and see the world.

technicalProjects.title: FLOW Lab Research (UC Berkeley)
technicalProjects.longDescription: Designed a physical enclosure for a high-sensitivity ME3 Photon Detector array used for flow regime analysis. Developed a Raspberry Pi Pico W-based cooling controller with PWM pump regulation and a visual/auditory alarm system to prevent thermal damage. Fabricated a custom air generation module with a high-efficiency fan funnel and MEMS velocity sensor.

technicalProjects.title: UCL Rocketry
technicalProjects.longDescription: Designed the ServoMag parachute ejection system, utilizing a servomotor and electromagnet for precise electronic actuation. Developed a dual-deployment recovery system with main and drogue parachutes, leading to a successful recovery and top-ranking at the Spaceport America Cup.

technicalProjects.title: UCL Mechathon
technicalProjects.longDescription: Collaborated in a five-member team to design and manufacture an elastic-band-powered aircraft within a 48-hour development cycle. Utilized Fusion 360 to model an aerodynamically optimized glider and employed laser cutting and 3D printing to achieve first runner-up status.

technicalProjects.title: Mathematical Modelling

subProjects.title: Population Modelling
subProjects.description: Fitted Malthusian and logistic growth models to two centuries of census data in MATLAB, estimating intrinsic growth rates and carrying capacity from real-world records.

subProjects.title: Pandemic Simulation
subProjects.description: Derived the SIR compartmental equations from first principles and simulated COVID-19 and H1N1 outbreak scenarios, quantified via least squares regression and Euler's method.

subProjects.title: Footbridge Dynamics
subProjects.description: Modelled pedestrian-induced lateral bridge vibration as a damped second-order ODE under square-wave gait forcing — solved with Fourier series and finite differences, closing with a sensitivity study across walking frequencies (0.7–1.2 Hz).

subProjects.title: Image Compression & Edge Detection
subProjects.description: Applied eigendecomposition and rank-r SVD to compress grayscale images, and vector calculus gradient operators for edge detection — visualising the fidelity/storage trade-off across compression levels.

technicalProjects.longDescription: A two-year arc of modelling coursework at UCL (ENGF0003 & ENGF0004), turning analytical mathematics into working MATLAB simulations of real systems. The work spans fitting logistic growth models to two centuries of population data, simulating epidemics with SIR compartmental models, predicting pedestrian-induced footbridge vibrations with Fourier series and finite-difference schemes, and compressing images via eigendecomposition and SVD.

technicalProjects.title: UCL Engineering Challenges
technicalProjects.longDescription: Engineered a 1kg balsa wood pylon using GSA Structural Analysis and truss theory. The design successfully sustained a record-breaking load of 235N during physical performance testing.

professionalAndLeadership.longDescription: Contributed to high-profile projects including a specialist research facility and two prominent London museums. Designed condensate routing for MVHR units using Dalux and conducted pressure duct calculations and sizing within BIM and Revit environments. Performed area scheduling and AHU service classification in Bluebeam Revu, and utilized Arup’s in-house tools for embodied carbon analysis of FCU servicing options.

I started SSI at the end of 2021 to show promising young Sarawakians what's possible after secondary school, and how to get there through the scholarships, loans and sponsorships many never hear about. What began as a central hub for post-secondary pathways and financial aid applications has grown, through years of grassroots work, into a youth organisation focused on access, advocacy and equality for every Sarawakian student.

papers.title: Implementation and Control of a Cooling Subsystem for an ME3 X-ray Photon Detector Enclosure
papers.abstract: Design, assembly, and control of a closed-loop coolant system for an X-ray photon detector — a temperature-banded PWM control scheme on a Raspberry Pi Pico 2W, a 180W thermoelectric heat exchanger loop, and validation against the detector's 40°C thermal safety threshold.

papers.title: Phonon-Glass Electron-Crystal (PGEC) Behaviour in Nanowire-Based Solid-State Heat Pumps for Residential Cooling
papers.abstract: Investigates silicon nanowire thermoelectrics as a refrigerant-free alternative to vapor-compression cooling, analysing how phonon-boundary scattering can decouple thermal and electrical conductivity to raise device efficiency.

papers.title: Effect of Hierarchy on the Mechanical Performance of Honeycomb Structures
papers.authors: with J. Merioles, Y. R. Ioriya, J. Kim, J. Park
papers.abstract: FEA comparison of standard versus first-order hierarchical honeycombs in carbon fiber-Onyx composite, quantifying effective stiffness, peak principal stress, and strain energy under in-plane and out-of-plane loading.

papers.title: The Accountability Gap in Autonomous Defense Systems: An Ethical Audit of U.S. Regulations and Engineering
papers.authors: with A. Wang, N. Luo, E. Wei
papers.abstract: An audit of how U.S. regulatory frameworks assign — and fail to assign — responsibility when autonomous weapons systems cause harm, and what that gap demands of the engineers who build them.
